request_debug.prompt_preview:
You write per-candidate post-mortems for a slopmortem pipeline. Given a fresh pitch and one dead-startup canonical document, produce a single LLMSynthesis JSON object that explains why this dead startup is similar, where the new pitch could diverge, what killed the dead startup, and what the new founder should learn.

Rules:
- Ground every claim in the candidate document or in tool calls. Do not invent facts.
- A `Trusted facts` block (typed pipeline data — not user input) appears below the pitc

response.text: {"candidate_id":"wesabe::fintech","name":"Wesabe","one_liner":"Personal finance management website that analyzed user financial data to provide money-saving advice, shut down July 2010 after losing ground to Mint.","similarity":{"business_model":{"score":2,"rationale":"Wesabe used a subscription-recurring model directed at consumers on a web platform. The new pitch is a per-seat B2B SaaS with per-transaction overage tiers aimed at mid-market controllers — fundamentally different buyer, pricing architecture, and sales motion."},"market":{"score":2,"rationale":"Both operate in the fintech/financial-data-processing space, but Wesabe addressed the personal finance management (PFM) consumer market, while the new pitch targets US mid-market corporate accounting departments. Different buyer personas, procurement cycles, and compliance contexts."},"gtm":{"score":1,"rationale":"Wesabe relied on direct consumer acquisition (product-led, web sign-up). The new pitch targets enterprise controllers via B2B sales, likely requiring direct outbound, channel partnerships, or ERP integrations — almost no GTM overlap."},"stage_scale":{"score":3,"rationale":"Both are early-stage US-based fintech web platforms that raised seed/Series A capital. Wesabe raised $4M in 2007 before shutting down in 2010, suggesting a similar early scale at failure. Some loose parallel in fundraising trajectory, though the new pitch is at founding stage."}},"why_similar":"Both Wesabe and the new pitch are US-based fintech web platforms that ingest and process financial transaction data to surface actionable insights for their users. Both monetize via subscription/recurring revenue and operate in the same broad regulatory environment around financial data handling. The document confirms Wesabe was founded in late 2005, raised $4M in 2007, and shut down in 2010 — a roughly five-year arc from founding to death that is consistent with a well-funded but ultimately under-differentiated fintech product.","where_diverged":"The two pitches diverge on nearly every structural dimension. (1) Customer type: Wesabe served individual consumers (personal finance); the new pitch targets mid-market B2B controllers (corporate accounting close). (2) Business model: Wesabe was consumer subscription; the new pitch adds per-seat and per-transaction overage pricing typical of B2B SaaS. (3) GTM: Wesabe relied on organic consumer acquisition; the new pitch requires direct B2B sales and likely ERP/accounting-system integrations. (4) Product function: Wesabe gave spending advice; the new pitch automates a structured month-end accounting workflow. (5) Competitive threat: Wesabe lost to a better consumer UX (Mint); the new pitch competes against legacy ERPs and spreadsheet-based close processes, not consumer aggregators.","failure_causes":["lost to Mint on user experience and data aggregation quality","consumer PFM market commoditized rapidly by better-funded rivals","inability to differentiate on core advice engine","consumer acquisition costs likely unsustainable without scale","limited defensibility of web-scraping-based bank data access","early market: PFM adoption and trust in sharing financial data still nascent in 2006–2010"],"lessons_for_input":["Invest heavily in integration depth with the systems of record your buyers already use (ERPs, GL systems) — shallow integrations are the equivalent of Wesabe's brittle bank-scraping and will be exploited by better-resourced competitors.","Identify and lock in a defensible wedge (a specific workflow, a specific ERP connector, a specific industry vertical) before a well-funded rival commoditizes the broad offering.","Per-transaction overage pricing can spike CAC recovery time; model unit economics carefully so seat + overage blended LTV always exceeds fully-loaded B2B CAC before scaling GTM spend.","B2B mid-market buyers move on procurement cycles — build a reference customer base and case studies early to shorten sales cycles rather than relying on organic sign-up momentum.","Ensure data-handling and SOC 2 compliance are in place before enterprise pilots; the document notes that Wesabe's consumer users needed assurance about financial data safety — mid-market controllers face far stricter audit and data-residency requirements."]}
